- Hardened that test in `baf5f30`. The first version asserted the token was absent from the error log without proving the log was written: on a clean fail-closed allow `writeError` never fires, so the array was empty and the check held for the wrong reason. It now pushes a malformed upstream line to reach the real `writeError` path, waits on the error callback rather than a sleep, and guards that the log is non-empty. The token is a random `base64url` value rather than a repeated character. Mutating `bin.ts` to swallow the line makes the test hang instead of pass, which is the intended failure direction. `Promise.withResolvers` is unavailable here because `tsconfig.base.json` pins `lib: es2022`, so the executor form is used.

## 2026-10-17 Harness lane: documents-tab u shortcut fixed, PTY regression gated

- Round six hunted unrun commands and found the PTY TUI regression dead:
  `pnpm run test:tui` is manual only and was not in the gate, so the
  10-11 TUI upgrade silently broke four of its markers and left the
  documents-tab undo shortcut dead for six days. Measured before the
  fix: after Enter (which now deliberately only inspects) pressing u
  processed at busy=false yet rendered only the notice "Select a
  document with an outstanding change", with no UNDO panel.
- Root cause: the inspect branch returns before documentPath is set, so
  `prepareUndo` searched operations against an unset path. Fixed in
  `packages/cli/src/tui/workspace.ts`: on the documents tab the
  selection is already the undo target, so the shortcut derives the
  session and path from the selected row. Read the outcome empirically
  through a monkeypatched DiffScreenWriter dump of the full frame.
- Verifier markers now match what the TUI renders (revision inspector
  field, the Undid transcript row after a search close because the
  search filter keeps the YOU row visible, PROPERTIES for the schema
  panel), its failure output carries the last full screen frame, and it
  pins the tool identity the workbench actually registers:
  `void_workspace_write`, not the `nomo_workspace_write` it expected
  (that spelling never existed in code). CODING-TOOLS-MAP.md and the
  desktop smoke at src-tauri/main.rs:332 still name nomo_: recorded in
  D-23 as a named leak for the explicit versioned migration.
- The regression joined the root gate as `script/tui-pty` (8 PASS
  lines; a missing python3 or pty module is named UNRUN, not a silent
  skip), so marker and shortcut drift now fails every run. Evidence:
  full gate 21 suites, 2969 tests, 0 fail, 0 UNRUN; TUI unit tests
  green with the new workspace-controls test (15/15 in that file).
  Commits `6fb93b2` and note `5fb567b`; origin/main equals lane head.

## OMP TUI visual benchmark audit, 2026-10-19

Scope is the approved read-only source and renderer-test audit. Reference source is the clean `v18.6.2` OMP checkout at `/Users/dawe/Developer/upstream/omp-src`; implementation is NOMO worktree `tui/omp-continuation`. OMP working tree is unchanged.

- Six comparison surfaces are confirmed: welcome and idle chat, user and assistant transcript blocks, tool lifecycle cards, settings, split list/detail with trees, and model selection. The first five share visual-system concerns. Model selection differs in authority and available data. OMP-only product actions are not parity targets.
- Welcome differs by product purpose: OMP centers its built-in logo and wordmark, version and optional tip; NOMO renders local workspace, model, project and agent context plus NOMO help. Preserve NOMO information and identity; the structural centering and available space are visual comparison targets, not a request to copy OMP branding.
- Transcript framing and Markdown structures are comparable. NOMO adds full-width user/assistant message frames and keeps tool/error rows outside. OMP user messages use a background-toned, headless bubble with optional host-provided actions. Event types and action availability differ, so compare hierarchy and wrapping, not exact labels or actions.
- Tool cards share lifecycle and bounded-output concepts. OMP has structured pending/running/done/error/cancelled status, duration and disclosure. NOMO's safe adapter renders requested/complete/error/unknown and bounded event summaries; raw arguments remain excluded. Status names cannot be mapped one-to-one without event-contract evidence.
- Settings layout is directionally comparable but not equivalent in ownership. OMP supports interactive section sidebar at wide widths when its content pane has at least 60 columns, and inline headings otherwise. NOMO uses a single authoritative catalog with explicit source, default, effective value and editability; only approved settings mutate. No new controls inferred from OMP.
- Split geometry: NOMO starts its two-pane layout at 120 columns, reserves a 7-column gap, assigns about 40 percent to inspector up to 68 columns. Calculated NOMO pane widths are 44/29 at 80 (stacked), 68/45 at 120, 92/61 at 160, and 125/68 at 200. OMP SplitPane is configurable by split threshold and minimum pane sizes, so a numeric match is not established from default source alone.
- Renderer/test evidence exists in NOMO `workspace.ts`, `message-frame.ts`, `tool-card.ts`, `settings.ts`, `split-pane.ts`; tests cover all 12 tabs at multiple widths, welcome rendering, frame widths, tree connectors, safe tool output and settings behavior. OMP source and tests cover welcome centering, narrow welcome cutoff, grouped settings fallback/sidebar and adaptive split geometry.
- Ran NOMO's existing `pnpm run tui:preview -- 80 24`; it rendered the static illustrative WRITE PATH fixture, not the OMP-equivalent chat surface. OMP source test execution was blocked by an incompatible cached `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils@18.11.2` export (`takeRecentLoopPhase`) against v18.6.2. No dependency install was attempted.
- Interactive PTY capture and screenshot comparison were not performed because they would require working outside the authorized worktree or creating an unapproved OMP worktree; user explicitly said capture is not required for this pass. Obsidian CLI was unavailable because the application is not running. No Graphify index update was performed; the existing vault graph is rooted at a different worktree.

Result: no new visual fix is justified from this read-only source/test audit alone. The broad shell and selection/detail redesign remains open in the plan. Color-depth behavior and proxy hold detail remain separately blocked pending approval.

## 2026-10-27: NOMO x YC startup plán a soukromá knihovna

Doplněno 23 zakladatelských dokumentů v `docs/strategy/`, včetně obecné produktové teze, produktové specifikace, tržního a konkurenčního přehledu, českého discovery a prodeje, LeadsPicker guardrailů, evaluace a ekonomiky, integrace NOMO, Own Your Intelligence, air-gapped varianty a integrované roadmapy. Vytvořen SVG plán v `docs/strategy/assets/2026-10-27-nomoyc-roadmap.svg`.

První trh je Česko; EU následuje po ověření. Dlouhodobou vizí je obecná firemní znalostní a pracovní platforma napříč obory. První placený pilot ale musí ověřit jeden konkrétní workflow. CFO je dostupný rozhovor, ne zvolená finanční vertikála. LeadsPicker podle zakladatele obsahuje seznam firem a veřejné či odvozené kontakty. Žádný marketingový e-mail z databáze nebyl autorizován ani odeslán. ÚOOÚ uvádí, že veřejně dostupný e-mail sám neopravňuje k nevyžádanému obchodnímu e-mailu: https://uoou.gov.cz/cinnost/obchodni-sdeleni/casto-kladene-otazky-k-zakonu-c-4802004-sb.

Strategie je v soukromém `Dawe583/nomo` main commit `fdcce501cbfdc3978ca82c1be02f1992c5f0482e`. Web je v `Dawe583/DavidSak` main commit `d139c77debfe393706885e6e831bee0c3d35f521`; produkční deployment je Ready. Zdrojový plán a dokumenty jsou šifrované AES-256-GCM; klíč je citlivá produkční proměnná Vercelu. API vrací plaintext až po ověřeném session cookie. Přihlášení v produkci otevřelo 23 dokumentů. Anonymní API vrací 401; přímý požadavek na `/api/_lib/nomoyc-private-content.js` vrací 404; `/nomoyc` má noindex, no-store a CSP. Homepage odkaz neobsahuje.

Tržní verdikt zůstává hypotéza: YC RFS a technická shoda nejsou důkaz poptávky. Neproběhl rozhovor, placený pilot ani ověření ochoty platit. Další krok je požádat CFO o rozhovor, zmapovat poslední konkrétní úkol a získat doporučení na operátora a experta.

This is a remote workflow/agent surface, not a model-completion API matching `gitlab-duo-agent`. Sources: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/duo_agent_platform_flows/, https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/agents/external/. No row change.

## 2026-11-02: H75 stale-lock recovery checkpoint

- Re-ran the four targeted `LocalStorage` lock fixtures under Node v24.14.1. Results: 3/4 passed, 1 failed. The deterministic test `storage refuses a lock replaced after the final stale-owner check` still fails at `packages/workbench/src/storage.test.ts:184` with `Missing expected exception`; its hook replaces the checked dead-owner lock with the current live PID immediately before `unlinkSync`, then the implementation deletes it and commits. This is a reproduced local race, not an inferred concern.
- The focused OpenAI account-store and lifecycle suites passed 13/13. This does not clear the separate lifecycle stale-replacement fixture from the preceding run, which reproduced the same missing rejection. No network/provider request or credential was used.
- Read the Node v24.14.1 filesystem implementation surface and current official Node fs, Node SQLite and SQLite locking/atomic-commit documentation. Node fs has pathname unlink, but no portable unlink-only-if-this-inode primitive. SQLite offers OS-managed transaction locking for participating processes, but cannot serialize legacy PID-lock processes that do not consult it. A cooperative recovery reservation has the same compatibility and stale-reservation problem. No implementation change is safe to claim under mixed old/new process compatibility.
- Updated the isolated worktree graph `.nomo/harness-work-state.json` and approved provider compatibility spec with the reproductions, source references, blocked decision and migration criteria. ## 2026-11-02: H75 lock sentinel review

- Two independent read-only reviews rejected a permanent directory sentinel as a mixed-version lock fix. Historical storage permits two stale reapers to validate dead lock F; process A can replace it with live lock G and enter save; process B can then unlink G using its earlier validation. A new process can acquire a directory sentinel after that unlink while A still writes. This is the same check-then-unlink race, not a safe conversion barrier.
- Safe sentinel conversion requires a quiescent cutover that stops every old writer and in-flight stale reaper before creating the sentinel. No supported rollout contract proves that condition. The current new runtime still fails closed on stale locks and preserves existing encrypted bytes; H75 remains blocked and H76 remains dependent.
- A disposable synthetic child-process probe showed two current account-lock processes do not overlap in one basic held-lock scenario. This is not full storage or refresh serialization evidence. A temporary node:test harness attempt hung and was removed; no production process or test edit remains.

## 2026-11-09 Streaming redraw proof-scan reduction

- `WorkspaceTui.refresh()` ignores trailing `message.delta` events for transcript-stability checks and reads the Workbench's in-memory `ledgerRevision()` before reusing verified proof state. The revision increments only after a successful persisted workspace commit, so a terminal status event that precedes its ledger write cannot leave proofs stale. Forced verification and ledger export still perform a fresh scan; proof errors remain fail-closed.
- `renderChatRows()` caches settled transcript rows and redraws only the streaming delta tail while the stable prefix, rendering options and event boundary remain unchanged. It rebuilds the prefix when a settled event arrives or the event window changes.
